title: Rakuten Securities breach, Nov 2026

subject.name: Rakuten Securities
subject.about: Rakuten Securities is a Japanese online brokerage, founded in 1999 and based in Tokyo, owned mostly by Rakuten's securities holding company with Mizuho Securities. People use it to trade Japanese and foreign shares, investment funds, FX and other products online.

also_called: 楽天証券 情報漏えい
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Rakuten Securities, Rakuten Group, Japan's Financial Services Agency, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: Rakuten Securities' Nov 24 second report says personal details of about 4.41 million people and login IDs of about 11.98 million accounts leaked. Press called it the largest breach at a Japanese securities firm so far.
who_is_affected: Current and former Rakuten Securities customers, and people who applied for an account but never opened one. The company says it has identified them and will tell them individually; it urges caution about phishing and suggests setting a passkey.

known.text: Rakuten Securities says a third party gained unauthorized access to some of its systems, detected on Nov 16.
It says information in its test environment leaked, first reported on Nov 17 as a possible leak on Nov 11.
Its Nov 24 second report says details of about 4.41 million people leaked, including birth dates and addresses, plus login IDs of 11.98 million accounts.
It says it has not confirmed any password or PIN leak, or related unauthorized trades.
The company says it used real customer data, not dummy data, in the test environment, the press reports.
Japan's Financial Services Agency ordered the company to report on Nov 19.

not_known.text: How the attacker got in, and what flaw was used.
Whether anyone has claimed a ransom or published the data.
Whether the company's statement that passwords and PINs were not leaked holds up.
Whether the real customer data in the test environment was masked: the company told one outlet it was not, but another reports it is still under investigation.
When and how the company will publish its investigation results, and whether it will offer compensation.
